use: Rules of a game, a house or a group; mamoru = follow them, yaburu = break them.

example.ja: ルールはちゃんと守ってよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Ruuru wa chanto mamotte kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: ルールはちゃんと守ってくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please make sure you follow the rules.

notes: Kisoku is the more formal word for regulations, like school rules.

use: Society in general, and especially adult working life after school.

example.ja: 社会に出れば分かるよ。
example.english: You'll get it once you're out in the real world.

examplePolite.ja: 社会に出れば分かりますよ。
examplePolite.english: You'll understand once you start working.

notes: Shakaijin = a working adult. At school, shakai is social studies.

use: Often in arguments: ... kenri wa nai = you have no right to ...

example.romaji: Anata ni sonna koto o iu kenri wa nai.
example.ja: あなたにそんなことを言う権利はない。
example.english: You have no right to say that.

examplePolite.romaji: Anata ni sonna koto o iu kenri wa arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: あなたにそんなことを言う権利はありません。
examplePolite.english: You have no right to say that.

notes: Kenri ga aru = have the right. Its pair is gimu (duty).

use: Said of rules (X wa kinshi = X isn't allowed) and ends many signs.

examplePolite.romaji: Koko wa tabako kinshi desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: ここはタバコ禁止ですよ。

notes: On signs: chuusha kinshi = no parking; satsuei kinshi = no photos.

use: Both the natural environment and the conditions where you live, work or study.

example.romaji: Ima no shokuba, kankyou ii yo.
example.english: My current workplace is a really nice environment.

examplePolite.romaji: Ima no shokuba wa kankyou ga ii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今の職場は環境がいいです。
examplePolite.english: My current workplace is a good environment.

notes: Kankyou mondai = environmental issues. Kankyou ga kawaru = your surroundings change, like a new job or school.

example.romaji: Kono machi, kekkou rekishi aru n da yo.
example.ja: この町、結構歴史あるんだよ。
example.english: This town actually has quite a bit of history.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono machi wa kekkou rekishi ga aru n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: この町は結構歴史があるんですよ。
examplePolite.english: This town has quite a long history.

notes: Rekishi ga aru = have a long history. Also the school subject.

use: Schooling and bringing up children; at work, training new staff.

example.romaji: Kodomo no kyouiku tte, okane kakaru yo ne.
example.ja: 子どもの教育って、お金かかるよね。
example.english: Kids' education really costs money, doesn't it?

examplePolite.romaji: Kodomo no kyouiku wa okane ga kakarimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 子どもの教育はお金がかかりますね。
examplePolite.english: Children's education is expensive, isn't it?

notes: Kyouiku suru = to educate or train someone. Shinjin kyouiku = training new hires.

use: News media and reporters, often said with a critical tone.

example.romaji: Masukomi tte, sugu oogesa ni iu yo ne.
example.ja: マスコミって、すぐ大げさに言うよね。
example.english: The media always blow things out of proportion, don't they?

examplePolite.romaji: Masukomi wa sugu oogesa ni iimasu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: マスコミはすぐ大げさに言いますよね。
examplePolite.english: The media do tend to exaggerate, don't they?

notes: From 'mass communication'. Media is also used and sounds more neutral.
